question: Fundamental Duties were incorporated in Part IV-A of the Constitution by the ________ Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
solution:
The correct answer is __**42nd**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Fundamental duties were added on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
 
• The committee suggested that the duty to pay taxes to be included in the fundamental duties
 
• The committee also recommended that the legislatures should prescribe law for imposing a penalty for violation of the duties.
 
 
• But paying taxes and penalty for violation duties are not incorporated in the constitution.
 
 
 
• Statement 3 is also not recommended by the committee because as per the recommendation the law made by legislatures to impose a penalty shall not be questioned in the court on the ground of infringement of any of fundamental rights. ​__
 
 

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Article
 Explanation
 
 
 
 

 Article 35
 This article gives the power to Parliament to determine the acts and laws that will govern who can be a citizen of India. It is divided into two parts - Article 35(a) and Article 35(b). It also empowers the parliament to limit or abrogate the fundamental rights of the armed forces, para-military forces, police forces, intelligence agencies and similar services where the maintenance of discipline is deemed to be of paramount importance.
 
 

 Article 47
 Article 47 falls under the directive principles of state policy. It states that the State has a duty to raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living and to improve public health. The State shall regard the raising of the level of nutrition and the standard of living of its people and the improvement of public health as among its primary duties and, in particular, the State shall endeavour to bring about prohibition of the consumption except for medicinal purposes of intoxicating drinks and of drugs which are injurious to health.
 
 

 Article 51
 This article is also part of the directive principles of state policy. It mandates that the State shall endeavor to: promote international peace and security, maintain just and honorable relations between nations, foster respect for international law and treaty obligations, and encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration.
